subtype: Approach: keep outside relationships and reality checks [Action]
passage:
Avni: Everyone says you were the only one who walked out. How?

Yamini: Honestly, I didn't walk out at first. What helped was that I kept ordinary things going. Every Sunday I still called home, and I still had dinner with my old roommate on Wednesdays. After each meeting I told them what the group had said. One night I repeated a line the leader liked, "doubt just means your ego is talking." My roommate laughed and said, "How convenient for whoever is saying it." I heard it from outside for the first time. The group kept telling me my family didn't understand me, but the calls sounded so normal, so unhurried, next to the meetings. That gap kept showing me what was off.

qa.q: How often did Yamini call home?
How did Yamini feel when the roommate laughed at the leader's line?
qa.a: Yamini was startled, then clearer: hearing the line from outside made it sound different.

qa.q: What else could Yamini do to keep a clear view, and why?
qa.a: Yamini could write down what the group asks for and compare it with what family and friends think, because a written record is harder to explain away.

qa.q: How might the roommate have felt hearing Yamini's updates?
qa.a: The roommate probably felt worried but glad to be trusted, and helped just by listening and asking plain questions.

grounding: Illustrates keeping weekly calls with family and old friends and discussing the group's claims with them, so outside views break the closed loop.
